SUPERSEDED AGAIN ON 10 NOVEMBER, AND THE FIGURES ABOVE ARE NOW THE 11.10.26 PACKAGE. SEVEN NUMBER SETS NOW EXIST FOR ONE ASSET IN THREE WEEKS, and this is the risk the page should carry loudest. In order: 20.3% / 2.25x / $11.65M / 6.69% (83 firms before 27 Oct); 21.5% / 2.33x / $11.77M / 5.71% (the GMass blast and CIM); 20.9% / 2.28x / $11.98M / 5.71% (Ackman-Ziff only, the broker fee grossed in); 21.1% / 2.30x / 9.0% / $11.77M / 5.94% (Zamir's own 30 Oct sends, including M Squared and Clairmont); 20.9% / 2.27x / 17.1% LP net / 5.58% (Kevin to Eldridge Acre, 5 Nov); 21.1% / 2.28x / 17.2% LP net / $11.73M / 5.51% (Kevin to Engle, 9 Nov); and now 21.1% / 2.28x / 16.2% LP net / $12.03M / 5.51%. The coupon has walked 6.69 to 5.94 to 5.71 to 5.58 to 5.51; the ask has walked $11.65M to $11.77M to $11.98M to $12.03M; and the LP net dropped a full point, 17.2% to 16.2%, in twenty-four hours. Several firms are mid-diligence on different files right now - Eldridge holds the 5 Nov set and has a call at 9 AM PT tomorrow, Engle holds the 9 Nov set, Clairmont and M Squared were sent the 30 Oct one. Two LPs comparing notes, or one LP reconciling an old email against a new model, finds a moving target. Decide which file is live and reissue to anyone still reading an old one.  **20 NOVEMBER 2026, 12:01 PM ET - A FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE PSA HAS BEEN SIGNED BY PURCHASER AND SENT FOR COUNTERSIGNATURE, AND IT MOVES EVERY DATE THIS BOARD HAS BEEN COUNTING DOWN TO.** Zach Oseland sent Ronny Hecht and Jim Lombardi (seller's counsel, Ross Banks) a First Amendment, executed by Purchaser, that EXTENDS DUE DILIGENCE TO 11 DECEMBER 2026, MOVES CLOSING TO 11 JANUARY 2027 AND SETS AN OUTSIDE CLOSING DATE OF 19 JANUARY 2027. It followed 'Ryan's email to Zamir this morning' - Ryan Epstein at Walker & Dunlop, the listing broker. IF THE SELLER COUNTERSIGNS, the $250,000 earnest money does NOT go hard today at 5 PM CT; refundability runs three more weeks, and the raise gets 21 extra days. It also closes the one-month gap this file has carried since 21 Oct between the contractual closing date (21 December) and what every piece of marketing says (January 2027) - the amendment makes the marketing correct rather than the contract. IT IS NOT DONE YET. The amendment is signed by Purchaser ONLY; Lombardi replied at 2:44 PM ET asking Zach for a phone call rather than returning a countersigned copy, which is neutral on its face but is not a yes. UNTIL A COUNTERSIGNED COPY LANDS, TREAT 20 NOV 5 PM CT AS STILL LIVE. Two diligence items Zach raised on 10 Nov were also still outstanding as of this morning and are worth closing out whichever way the dates land: the Exhibit I discrepancies (the Waste Connections agreement dated 4/18/2024 against Exhibit I's 7/21/2023, and the TXU common-meter contract dated 12/14/2023 whose term ended 5/31/2026 against Exhibit I's 12/14/2024), and the Paragraph 8(a)(vii) written disclosure of pending personal injury claims, which Seller owed before the DD period expired and had not delivered.  **20 NOV 3:40 PM ET - SELLER'S COUNSEL HAS REDLINED THE AMENDMENT RATHER THAN SIGNED IT, AND THE CHANGES ARE NOT COSMETIC.** Jim Lombardi called Zach, then sent a revised amendment and a Litera redline ('[Seller v111202026]'), expressly 'subject to my client's review and comment', to Zach and Ronny Hecht at the same time 'in the interest of time'. BOTH SIGNATURE BLOCKS ON THE REVISED DRAFT ARE BLANK, so ZMR's 12:01 PM execution no longer attaches and Purchaser has to re-sign whatever lands. At 3:40 PM ET there were EIGHTY MINUTES to the 5:00 PM CT expiry of the current Due Diligence Period, and nothing was executed. SELLER ACCEPTS THE DATES. The core of what ZMR asked for survives: Due Diligence to 5:00 PM CT Friday 11 December 2026, Closing Monday 11 January 2027, and the Deposit expressly 'remains refundable to Purchaser as provided in the Agreement until the expiration of the Due Diligence Period as so extended'. WHAT SELLER ADDED IS A SET OF WAIVERS AND ONE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, AND THEY ARE ZACH'S CALL, NOT A SUMMARY POINT. (1) Section 2 now carves two things out of the extension: the Paragraph 5(c) Service Contracts cancellation notice is NOT extended and Purchaser's election before the Amendment Date is final; and Purchaser acknowledges Seller 'has delivered or made available' every Paragraph 5(a) item, with the Due Diligence Period 'not to be further extended under Paragraph 5(a) or otherwise'. (2) Section 4 prices the outside date: the extension to 19 January is a one-time option needing written notice by Monday 4 January and a FURTHER $100,000 deposit by Tuesday 5 January - a Closing Date Extension Fee that did not exist before. (3) Section 5 rewrites the title mechanics: Seller's response to the 13 November Title Objection Letter is due 4 December; the Title Review Period is extended to Wednesday 2 December, which is SHORTER than the Friday 4 December in ZMR's draft; further objections are limited to matters first disclosed in an updated Commitment or Survey, with everything else in the Title Documents 'approved by Purchaser'; and if Purchaser does not terminate by 5:00 PM CT on 11 December it is 'deemed to have waived such Title Objections and elected to proceed with the Closing'. (4) Section 6 adds, to the ratification clause, that 'Purchaser acknowledges that, as of the Amendment Date, to Purchaser's knowledge, Seller is not in default under the Agreement, and Purchaser has no claim against Seller under the Agreement.' THAT LAST ONE SITS DIRECTLY ON TOP OF TWO ITEMS SELLER STILL OWES. Zach wrote on 10 November asking Seller to reconcile the Exhibit I discrepancies (Waste Connections dated 4/18/2024 against Exhibit I's 7/21/2023; the TXU common-meter contract dated 12/14/2023 whose term ended 5/31/2026 against Exhibit I's 12/14/2024) and reminding Seller that under Paragraph 8(a)(vii) it must disclose any pending personal injury claims IN WRITING before the Due Diligence Period expires - 'We have not received anything yet.' As of this afternoon neither had been answered. Section 2 does at least pull 8(a)(vii) into the extended period, so that deadline moves with the rest; but signing a no-default, no-claim acknowledgement and a 5(a) full-delivery acknowledgement while those two items are outstanding is a question for ZMR's General Counsel before execution, not after. NOTHING HERE IS SIGNED. Until a fully executed copy exists, the operative dates remain the ORIGINAL ones: Due Diligence expiring 5:00 PM CT on 20 November 2026 and the $250,000 going hard.
